# Your armemon app guide

This file explains your app and every armemon command.

- Every command is ready to copy and paste.
- Run commands from inside your app folder.
- If your terminal says `armemon: command not found`, install the CLI once with
  `npm install -g @armemon-library/cli` — or put `npx @armemon-library/cli` in front,
  like `npx @armemon-library/cli doctor`.
- `memon` is a shorter name for the same command — `memon doctor` works exactly like
  `armemon doctor`.

## Quick start

```bash
# see every command
armemon --help

# add a screen
armemon create-screen Profile

# check that everything is set up
armemon doctor
```

## Your folders

| Folder | What goes there | Who changes it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `armemon/` | Settings for navigation, Redux, theme and plugins | armemon (you can too) |
| `src/screens/` | Your screens, one folder each | You |
| `src/shared/` | Components and hooks more than one screen uses | You |
| `src/store/slices/` | Your Redux state | You |

**One simple rule:** armemon updates the files in `armemon/`. Files in `src/` are
yours — armemon creates them once and never touches them again.

## Everyday tasks

### Add a screen

```bash
armemon create-screen Profile
```

This creates the screen, adds it to your navigator, and gives it a web address:
`/Profile`.

### Add a screen with an ID in its address, like /order/42

```bash
armemon create-screen Order --params "id:string" --link order/:id
```

### Rename or remove a screen

```bash
armemon rename-screen Profile Account
armemon remove-screen Account
```

### Give every screen a web address

If every screen opens at `localhost:5173` with nothing after it, run:

```bash
armemon link init
```

### See or change web addresses

```bash
armemon link list
armemon link add Profile me
armemon link remove Profile
```

### Add app state (Redux)

```bash
armemon create-slice cart
```

Then use it in any screen:

```tsx
import { useSelector, useDispatch } from '@armemon-library/redux';

const cart = useSelector((state: any) => state.cart.value);
const dispatch = useDispatch();
dispatch({ type: 'cart/set', payload: ['apple'] });
```

### Rename or remove app state

```bash
armemon rename-slice cart basket
armemon remove-slice basket
```

### Add a component or a hook

```bash
# used by many screens
armemon create-component ProductCard --shared

# used by one screen only
armemon create-component ProductRow --screen Order

armemon create-hook useCart --shared
```

These only create the file. Import it yourself where you need it.

### Change a setting

```bash
armemon set ui.themeMode dark
armemon set ui.brandColor "#ff6600"
armemon set essentials.notifications.position bottom
```

### Try a command without saving anything

Add `--dry-run` to any command that changes files:

```bash
armemon create-screen Profile --dry-run
```

### After you edit files in armemon/ yourself

```bash
armemon sync
```

This tidies the files so the next command can read them, and updates this guide.

You can edit anything in `armemon/`. The one file armemon rewrites completely is this
guide — so keep your own notes somewhere else.

### Update armemon's packages

After updating the CLI itself, run this inside your app:

```bash
armemon upgrade
```

It moves the app to the package versions that match the CLI, installs them, and tidies
the files in `armemon/`.

### Something is not working

```bash
armemon doctor
```

It checks your setup and tells you exactly what to fix.

## Plugins

Plugins add features to your app. Your app may use some or all of them.

### Add or remove a plugin

```bash
# what there is, and what this app has
armemon plugin list

# add one — set up exactly as choosing it at init would have
armemon plugin add redux

# take one out again
armemon plugin remove redux
```

Nothing changes until every step is worked out. Removing deletes only files that are
still exactly as armemon wrote them, and stops while your code still uses something it
would take away — it tells you what, and where. Add `--dry-run` to see the whole change
first.

### UI — theme, text and buttons

```tsx
import { Text, Button, Container, useTheme } from '@armemon-library/ui';

export default function HomeScreen() {
  const { mode } = useTheme();

  return (
    <Container>
      <Text level="large">Hello</Text>
      <Text muted>The theme is {mode}</Text>
      <Button label="Save" onPress={() => {}} />
    </Container>
  );
}
```

- Text sizes: `small`, `medium`, `large`, `xlarge`.
- Settings file: `armemon/ui/theme.config.ts`

### Redux — app state

The example is in "Add app state" above. You also get `createSlice`,
`createAsyncThunk` and `nanoid` from `@armemon-library/redux`.

- Settings file: `armemon/redux/store.config.ts`

### Navigation — screens and web addresses

Move to another screen:

```tsx
import { useNavigation } from '@react-navigation/native';

export function GoToProfile() {
  const navigation = useNavigation();
  return () => navigation.navigate('Profile');
}
```

- Settings folder: `armemon/navigation/`

### Essentials — messages, network and loading

```tsx
import { useNotifications, useNetworkStatus, useLoading } from '@armemon-library/essentials';

export function useSaveButton() {
  const { notify } = useNotifications();
  const { isOnline } = useNetworkStatus();
  const { showLoading, hideLoading } = useLoading();

  return async () => {
    if (!isOnline) {
      notify({ message: 'You are offline', type: 'warning' });
      return;
    }
    showLoading();
    notify({ message: 'Saved', type: 'success' });
    hideLoading();
  };
}
```

- Message types: `success`, `error`, `info`, `warning`.
- Settings file: `armemon/essentials/essentials.config.ts`

### Splash — the screen shown while the app starts

Change the colour and logo in `armemon/splash/splash.config.ts`.

## Use the plugins without the armemon CLI

You don't need the CLI. The plugins are normal npm packages, so you can add them to
any React Native app.

### Step 1 — install

Always install core:

```bash
npm install @armemon-library/core
```

Then add only the plugins you want:

```bash
# UI
npm install @armemon-library/ui

# Redux
npm install @armemon-library/redux @reduxjs/toolkit react-redux

# Redux, if you also want to save state when the app closes (optional)
npm install redux-persist @react-native-async-storage/async-storage

# Navigation
npm install @armemon-library/navigation @react-navigation/native @react-navigation/native-stack react-native-screens react-native-safe-area-context

# Essentials
npm install @armemon-library/essentials

# Essentials, if you also want network status (optional)
npm install @react-native-community/netinfo
```

### Step 2 — set up your plugins in one file

```ts
// armemon.setup.ts
import { registerRuntimeConfig } from '@armemon-library/core';
import { configureUiPlugin } from '@armemon-library/ui';
import { configureReduxPlugin } from '@armemon-library/redux';
import { configureEssentialsPlugin } from '@armemon-library/essentials';

registerRuntimeConfig({
  plugins: [
    configureUiPlugin({ themeMode: 'auto', brandColor: '#5eead4' }),
    configureReduxPlugin({ slices: {} }),
    configureEssentialsPlugin(),
  ],
  userTasks: [],
});
```

Only list the plugins you installed.

### Step 3 — wrap your app

```tsx
// App.tsx
import './armemon.setup';
import { KitProvider } from '@armemon-library/core';
import HomeScreen from './src/screens/HomeScreen';

export default function App() {
  return (
    <KitProvider>
      <HomeScreen />
    </KitProvider>
  );
}
```

### Want network status?

Essentials only checks the network when you give it `netInfoAdapter`. Install
`@react-native-community/netinfo` (Step 1), then:

```ts
// armemon.setup.ts
import { registerRuntimeConfig } from '@armemon-library/core';
import { configureEssentialsPlugin } from '@armemon-library/essentials';
import { netInfoAdapter } from '@armemon-library/essentials/netinfo';

registerRuntimeConfig({
  plugins: [configureEssentialsPlugin({ netInfoAdapter })],
  userTasks: [],
});
```

Now `useNetworkStatus()` reports whether the device is really online.

### Common mistakes

- **"No armemon runtime config registered"** — `import './armemon.setup';` must be at
  the top of `App.tsx`, above everything else.
- **"no NetInfo adapter was provided"** — you turned the network check on with
  `network: { enabled: true }` but didn't pass `netInfoAdapter`. Pass it as shown in
  "Want network status?" above.
- `plugins` and `userTasks` are both required. Use `[]` when you have none.
- The CLI commands in this guide (`armemon create-screen` and the rest) need an app
  made with `armemon init`. Without the CLI, you add screens and state yourself.

Two commands never change `armemon/`: `armemon create-component` and
`armemon create-hook` only create one file in `src/`.

The full list of commands and options is below.

---

# All commands and options

This list is made from the armemon CLI itself, so it always matches the version you have.

## Quick list

- `armemon init` — Scaffold a new app
- `armemon add` — Add a platform target to an app you already scaffolded
- `armemon create-screen` — Create a screen and register it in your navigator, param list and deep links
- `armemon remove-screen` — Remove a screen: unregister it, drop its types and deep link, delete its folder
- `armemon rename-screen` — Rename a screen everywhere: folder, component, route, types, deep link and navigate() calls
- `armemon plugin` — Add a plugin to this app, or take one out
- `armemon list` — List the plugins armemon can install (the same as armemon plugin list)
- `armemon doctor` — Check a scaffolded app's armemon wiring
- `armemon sync` — Re-align armemon's managed files, and move a legacy src/armemon/ to armemon/
- `armemon upgrade` — Move the app's @armemon-library packages to this CLI's versions, then sync
- `armemon create-slice` — Create a Redux slice and register it in your store config
- `armemon remove-slice` — Unregister a Redux slice and delete its file
- `armemon rename-slice` — Rename a Redux slice: its file, binding, store entry and action prefix
- `armemon link` — Read and edit the app's deep links
- `armemon set` — Set one option in a plugin's config
- `armemon create-component` — Create a component in a screen folder or the shared one (nothing is wired up)
- `armemon create-hook` — Create a hook in a screen folder or the shared one (nothing is wired up)

## Options that work on most commands

Each command below lists exactly which of these it takes.

| Option | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--dry-run` | Show what would change, but save nothing. Always safe to try |
| `--dir <path>` | Run on a different app folder, like `--dir ./MyApp` |
| `--json` | Print the result as JSON, for scripts and CI |
| `--all-accept` | Ask no questions and use the defaults |
| `--no-verify` | Skip the checks armemon runs after a change. Faster |
| `--force` | Do it even when armemon would normally stop. Each command below says when |
| `--help` | Show help for that command in your terminal |

When a command fails, it tells you what went wrong and how to fix it. For more detail,
put `ARMEMON_DEBUG=1` in front of the command.

## JSON output, for scripts

With `--json`, a command prints one JSON object on stdout and nothing else. Every one
starts with the same two fields:

- `schemaVersion` — the version of the output's shape, now `1`. It only changes
  when a field is removed or changes meaning, so skip fields you don't recognise.
- `ok` — `true` when the command did everything it was asked. The exit code agrees:
  `0` when ok, `1` for a problem, `130` when it was cancelled.

When a command fails, the object is `{ "ok": false, "error": { "message": "…", "hint": "…" } }`.

## Commands

### `armemon init`

Scaffold a new app

| Subcommand | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `init react-native` | Scaffold a new React Native app |

### `armemon init react-native [appName]`

Scaffold a new React Native app

| Argument | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `[appName]` | App name — letters and numbers, starting with a letter *(optional — you are asked if you leave it out)* |

| Flag | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--rn-version <version>` | React Native version (e.g. 0.76.0, or "latest") |
| `--pm <manager>` | Package manager: npm, yarn, pnpm or bun |
| `--language <lang>` | ts \| js (React Native ships no JS template; armemon converts) |
| `--logo <path>` | Splash logo image, relative to where you run this |
| `--platforms <list>` | Comma-separated: ios,android,web,windows,macos |
| `--plugins <list>` | Comma-separated plugin ids or package names (empty string for none) |
| `--all-accept` | Skip every prompt: every platform, every recommended plugin, and each question's own default |
| `--dry-run` | Print the resolved configuration and exit without writing anything |
| `--no-verify` | Skip armemon's own checks on the finished app (they run by default) |
| `--verify` | Run those checks (the default; accepted for explicitness) |
| `--json` | Print only a JSON summary on stdout (implies --all-accept) |

```bash
armemon init react-native MyApp
# every prompt answered with its default, every recommended plugin
armemon init react-native MyApp --all-accept
# pinned for CI, nothing interactive
armemon init react-native MyApp --pm pnpm --language ts --platforms ios,android,web --plugins redux,navigation --json
# see what it would do first
armemon init react-native MyApp --dry-run
```

### `armemon add <platform>`

Add a platform target to an app you already scaffolded

| Argument | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `<platform>` | Platform to add: ios, android, web, windows, macos |

| Flag | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--dir <path>` | The app directory (defaults to the nearest one at or above here) |
| `--dry-run` | List what adding the platform would do, without changing anything |
| `--no-verify` | Skip armemon's checks on the result (they run by default) |
| `--json` | Print only a JSON summary on stdout (implies --all-accept) |
| `--all-accept` | Take every default instead of asking |

```bash
armemon add web
armemon add windows --dir ./MyApp
armemon add ios --json
```

### `armemon create-screen [name]`

Create a screen and register it in your navigator, param list and deep links

| Argument | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `[name]` | Screen name — Order, OrderScreen, or order-history *(optional — you are asked if you leave it out)* |

| Flag | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--dir <path>` | The app directory (defaults to the nearest one at or above here) |
| `--full` | Create components/, hooks/, utils/ and assets/ folders |
| `--flat` | Create only index — no subfolders |
| `--register` | Register without asking; fail if there is no navigator |
| `--no-register` | Don't touch the navigator |
| `--navigator <name>` | Where to register: stack, tabs, drawer, a variable like Tab, or File:Variable |
| `--link <path>` | Deep-link path, e.g. order or order/:id |
| `--no-link` | Don't add a deep-link entry |
| `--params <list>` | Route params, e.g. "id:string,page?:number" (string, number, boolean) |
| `--initial` | Make it the navigator's initial route |
| `--modal` | Present it as a modal (stack navigators) |
| `--title <title>` | Header / tab title |
| `--force` | Replace the screen if it already exists |
| `--dry-run` | Show every change as a diff without writing anything |
| `--no-verify` | Skip armemon's checks on the result (they run by default) |
| `--json` | Print only a JSON summary on stdout (implies --all-accept) |
| `--all-accept` | Take every default instead of asking |

```bash
armemon create-screen Order
# typed route params, and a deep link that carries them
armemon create-screen Order --params "id:string,page?:number" --link order/:id
# a modal with a header title, in a stack
armemon create-screen Settings --modal --title Settings
# into a specific navigator, as its first route
armemon create-screen Feed --navigator Tab --initial
# just the file: no subfolders, no navigator, no link
armemon create-screen Order --flat --no-register --no-link
# look before writing, then do it without the checks
armemon create-screen Order --dry-run
armemon create-screen Order --json --no-verify
```

### `armemon remove-screen <name>`

Remove a screen: unregister it, drop its types and deep link, delete its folder

| Argument | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `<name>` | Screen name — Order, OrderScreen, or order-history |

| Flag | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--dir <path>` | The app directory (defaults to the nearest one at or above here) |
| `--keep-files` | Unregister it but keep its folder |
| `--force` | Remove it even while code still navigates to it, or it is an initial route |
| `--dry-run` | Show every change as a diff without writing anything |
| `--no-verify` | Skip armemon's checks on the result (they run by default) |
| `--json` | Print only a JSON summary on stdout (implies --all-accept) |
| `--all-accept` | Take every default instead of asking |

```bash
armemon remove-screen Order
# unregister it but keep the folder
armemon remove-screen Order --keep-files
# remove it even though something still navigates to it
armemon remove-screen Order --force
armemon remove-screen Order --dry-run
```

### `armemon rename-screen <from> <to>`

Rename a screen everywhere: folder, component, route, types, deep link and navigate() calls

| Argument | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `<from>` | The screen to rename — Order, OrderScreen, or order |
| `<to>` | Its new name |

| Flag | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--dir <path>` | The app directory (defaults to the nearest one at or above here) |
| `--link <path>` | A new deep-link path |
| `--keep-link` | Keep the current deep-link path even if it came from the old name |
| `--dry-run` | Show every change as a diff without writing anything |
| `--no-verify` | Skip armemon's checks on the result (they run by default) |
| `--json` | Print only a JSON summary on stdout (implies --all-accept) |
| `--all-accept` | Take every default instead of asking |

```bash
armemon rename-screen Order Invoice
# rename, and give it a new URL at the same time
armemon rename-screen Order Invoice --link invoice/:id
# rename, but leave the deep-link path alone
armemon rename-screen Order Invoice --keep-link
```

Add a plugin, wired in exactly as init would have

### `armemon link`

Read and edit the app's deep links

| Subcommand | What it does |
| --- | --- |

### `armemon link init`

Create a deep-link config covering every screen this app already has

| Flag | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--dry-run` | Show what would be created without writing anything |
| `--dir <path>` | The app directory (defaults to the nearest one at or above here) |
| `--json` | Print only a JSON summary on stdout |
| `--all-accept` | Take every default instead of asking |

```bash
# for an app scaffolded without deep linking: gives every screen a URL
armemon link init
armemon link init --dry-run
```

### `armemon link list`

Show every deep link, and where each one sits

| Flag | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--dir <path>` | The app directory (defaults to the nearest one at or above here) |
| `--json` | Print only a JSON summary on stdout |
| `--all-accept` | Take every default instead of asking |

```bash
armemon link list
armemon link list --json
```

### `armemon link add [route] [path]`

Add or update a deep link, nested under the right navigator

| Argument | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `[route]` | Route name — Order *(optional — you are asked if you leave it out)* |
| `[path]` | URL path — order/:id *(optional — you are asked if you leave it out)* |

| Flag | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--dry-run` | Show the change as a diff without writing anything |
| `--dir <path>` | The app directory (defaults to the nearest one at or above here) |
| `--json` | Print only a JSON summary on stdout |
| `--all-accept` | Take every default instead of asking |

```bash
armemon link add Order order/:id
# change the path a route already has
armemon link add Home start
```


### `armemon set [option] [value]`

Set one option in a plugin's config

| Argument | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `[option]` | Plugin option — ui.themeMode, essentials.notifications.position *(optional — you are asked if you leave it out)* |
| `[value]` | The value — dark, 18, true *(optional — you are asked if you leave it out)* |

| Flag | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--dir <path>` | The app directory (defaults to the nearest one at or above here) |
| `--raw` | Use the value as code rather than inferring a literal (e.g. __DEV__) |
| `--force` | Replace a value that is a function or a call |
| `--dry-run` | Show the change as a diff without writing anything |
| `--no-verify` | Skip armemon's checks on the result (they run by default) |
| `--json` | Print only a JSON summary on stdout (implies --all-accept) |
| `--all-accept` | Take every default instead of asking |

```bash
armemon set ui.themeMode dark
armemon set ui.baseFontSize 18
# a nested option
armemon set essentials.notifications.position bottom
# an expression rather than a literal
armemon set redux.devTools __DEV__ --raw
# replace a value that is currently a function
armemon set redux.middleware undefined --force
```

### `armemon create-component [name]`

Create a component in a screen folder or the shared one (nothing is wired up)

| Argument | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `[name]` | Component name — OrderRow *(optional — you are asked if you leave it out)* |

| Flag | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--dir <path>` | The app directory (defaults to the nearest one at or above here) |
| `--screen <name>` | Put it in that screen's own folder |
| `--shared` | Put it in the shared folder |
| `--force` | Replace the file if it already exists |
| `--dry-run` | Show what would be created without writing anything |
| `--json` | Print only a JSON summary on stdout (implies --all-accept) |
| `--all-accept` | Take every default instead of asking |

```bash
armemon create-component OrderRow
# into one screen's own components/ folder
armemon create-component OrderRow --screen Order
# into src/shared/components/, for something more than one screen uses
armemon create-component OrderRow --shared
```

### `armemon create-hook [name]`

Create a hook in a screen folder or the shared one (nothing is wired up)

| Argument | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `[name]` | Hook name — useOrderTotals *(optional — you are asked if you leave it out)* |

| Flag | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--dir <path>` | The app directory (defaults to the nearest one at or above here) |
| `--screen <name>` | Put it in that screen's own folder |
| `--shared` | Put it in the shared folder |
| `--force` | Replace the file if it already exists |
| `--dry-run` | Show what would be created without writing anything |
| `--json` | Print only a JSON summary on stdout (implies --all-accept) |
| `--all-accept` | Take every default instead of asking |

```bash
armemon create-hook useOrderTotals
armemon create-hook useOrderTotals --screen Order
armemon create-hook useSession --shared
```
